correctness.rationale: Direct matrix expansion proves exact fixed spectrum; elementary squared inequalities keep all six off-diagonal rates positive throughout the parameter interval. Row and column sums enforce unique uniform stationarity; the exit-rate sum gives activity 2 and each rate is bounded. The three identical edge currents yield the exact EPR expression and a logarithmic divergence as one positive reverse rate tends to zero. Continuity establishes every finite EPR value. A two-state chain has zero current by stationarity, proving sharp minimal dimension. The standalone SymPy checker passes 819 assertions; finite tests are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the explicit smallest-dimension strictly positive-rate Markov family with exactly fixed full simple real spectrum, uniform stationary probabilities, fixed global activity, bounded exit rates and a surjective entropy-production range [0,infinity). The 2026 Kolchinsky–Ohga–Ito paper constrains nonreal eigenmodes; Shiraishi 2026 constructs a large layered model refuting lower spectral dissipation bounds for complex modes; the 2024 Kolchinsky–Ohga–Ito result compares each nonequilibrium spectrum with its own additive reversibilization and gives lower bounds. None of these implications yields this full-spectrum fixed-activity unbounded-upper-dissipation example. A general unlocated inverse-spectral result remains a possible stronger implication.
residual_risks: General inverse eigenvalue realizations for doubly balanced Markov matrices or hidden-dissipation constructions might imply this three-state family even without matching words.
Some related papers were inspected by relevant theorem statements/sections rather than all appendices, and the Dechant 2021 paper was abstract-only.
A claim of uniqueness of the construction or complete novelty throughout mathematical physics is not made.
